text: GEOSPATIAL WORKS OUR ENGINEERING PROJECTS 21 Project Name : Construction of Necessary Number of Ticket Counters, Modernization of Passenger Waiting Rooms, Provision of Standard Toilet Facilities, Improvement of Drainage System, and Development of Passageways at Gabtoli Inter-District Bus Terminal under Dhaka North City Corporation . Duration: June 2026 – September 2026 Project Description : The project involved digital surveying and comprehensive improvement planning of Gabtoli Bus Terminal, Dhaka. The drone survey was incorporated covering 58.527 acres and 0.236 sq km. The scope of work included the design of two terminal buildings, expansion and reorganization of bus counters, development of an efficient bus circulation plan, improvement of the existing drainage system, and provision of new storm-water drainage lines. The project also included drainage system design, preparation of detailed design drawings, and Bill of Quantities (BOQ) to support cost estimation and future implementation. The overall objective was to improve terminal functionality, passenger facilities, bus movement efficiency, and storm-water management.

Project Duration: April 2025- May 2025 Project Description: The project involved the structural design and preparation of drawings for the LTP (Landfill Treatment Plant) of the sanitary landfill under the Moheshkhali Solid Waste Management (SWM) project. GEOSPATIAL WORKS OUR GEOSPATIAL PROJECTS 32 Project Name: Pilot Research Project on Irrigation Management and Web-based Agricultural Information System for Bangladesh (WEB-AIS) under Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC). Project Description: The WEB-AIS pilot projectaims to improve irrigation management and agricultural planning through an integrated geospatial information system. Covering approximately 208.37 km² across 23 unions and 260 mouzas in the Manikganj region, the project involved GNSS/RTK surveying, UAV-based mapping, photogrammetric processing, and cadastral map digitization. Key outputs include high-resolution orthomosaics , elevation models, land-cover maps, irrigation networks, and groundwater pump inventories. The database documents 142.02 km² of agricultural land, 536.12 km of irrigation canals, and 9,834 irrigation pumps, providing essential spatial information for efficient water-resource management, evidence-based irrigation planning, and sustainable agricultural development.. text: GEOSPATIAL WORKS 28 Project Name: Installation of Water-Level Gauge Readers and Topographic Surveying at Three Locations in Gangarampur under the WEB-AIS Project of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC). Project Description: The project involved the installation and adjustment of river water level gauge readers at three monitoring locations in Gangarampur Union, Batiaghata Upazila, Khulna District, Bangladesh, under the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC). The scope of work included conducting levelling surveys to establish accurate Reduced Levels (RLs), performing Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GNSS observations to determine precise geographic coordinates and elevations, and establishing temporary benchmarks to ensure reliable geodetic control. The project also involved measuring existing water depths, constructing bamboo support platforms, and installing gauge readers at the Jhopjhopia River, Guiyer Canal Opening near Amtola Canal, and the Y-section point of Guiyer Canal. GEOSPATIAL WORKS OUR QUICK DELIVERY PROJECTS 34 Project Name: The Abdulpur Railway Bypass under subproject 2 Rai lway Connectivity Improvement Preparatory Facility (RCIPF) Project (ADB Loan No: 6030 BAN) Project Description: The Abdulpur Railway Bypass Project involved a comprehensive topographic and physical feature survey across approximately 40 acres in Lalpur Upazila, Natore District, to support feasibility assessment, railway alignment planning, and detailed engineering design. The methodology integrated UAV photogrammetry, RTK GNSS, and Electronic Total Station (ETS) surveys, using 17 Ground Control Points (GCPs) and high-resolution imagery acquired by a DJI Matrice 4E UAV. Photogrammetric processing and GIS/CAD analysis generated georeferenced orthomosaics , DSM, DTM, 20 cm interval contour maps, cross-sections, LULC maps, utility maps, and railway infrastructure maps. Field observations documented existing terrain, railway infrastructure, roads, buildings, drainage networks, utilities, and property boundaries. The resulting geospatial database provide reliable spatial information with consistent centimetre-level vertical accuracy. Duration: August 2026 (Within 14 Days)

text: GEOSPATIAL WORKS Total Station Geospatial Works operates multi-brands (Topcon, Sokkia, CHCNAV, Kolida ) total stations for precise surveying and engineering measurement. These instruments support field surveying operations requiring accurate angle and distance measurements for topographic mapping, land surveys, construction layout, and engineering applications . Level Machine Geospatial Works utilizes Sokkia and Topcon automatic optical levels for precise elevation measurement and levelling operations. These instruments support the establishment and transfer of benchmarks, site levelling, road and drainage surveys, earthwork assessment, and construction projects requiring reliable vertical control. Eco Sounder Geospatial Works uses an echo sounder for hydrographic surveying and underwater depth measurement. When integrated with GNSS positioning and appropriate survey processing, depth measurements can be used to develop georeferenced bathymetric information for engineering and water-resource projects.
